title: The Singhs Endure the Siege of the Lion Cave

blocks.text: The Mughal assault on the cave becomes methodical as the attackers pour smoke into the opening, force villagers to dig, and then look for new ways to make the hiding place unlivable. Pressure from outside is relentless, but the trapped Singhs answer with the same stubborn improvisation that has marked the entire episode.

Within that struggle, the Singhs block the opening against smoke and fire by sealing gaps, using cloth and damp material, and refusing to panic while the siege intensifies. Their defense is as much moral as physical, because each improvised barrier declares that they will not simply be flushed out like animals.

Local villagers also slow the attackers by dragging out the labor demanded of them, and nightfall finally breaks the immediate momentum of the operation. The page therefore preserves the cave episode as a contest of patience in which Khalsa resolve repeatedly frustrates superior force.
